subject: Proposal: compact pod model + handling performance exceptions
messages:
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
To: lauren.bishop@redwood.com, vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com
Cc: marcus.lin@redwood.com
Date: 2027-05-09 08:12 -0700
Subject: Proposal: compact pod model + handling performance exceptions

Team —

After the last leadership review and several 1:1s with ICs and managers, I put together a concise proposal for a compact pod model aimed at tightening spans of control for compute-facing teams while keeping career scope intact. High-level goals: reduce cross-pod coordination load, preserve technical ladders, and create a small, standard process for performance exceptions so we don't confuse managers or publicly surface sensitive cases.

Key bullets:
- Move from (avg) 9 direct reports -> target avg 6 for pod leads in inference/runtime clusters.
- Define two pod sizes: Core Pods (4–6 people) and Expansion Pods (7–9 people) with clear ramp criteria.
- Create a two-week calibration window where managers can raise performance exceptions and request a short, documented intervention (coaching + paired objectives) before HR involvement.
- Quiet-transition checklist for roles we expect to backfill with minimal external comms (sensitive customer-facing infra roles).

Attached: compact-pod-rationale.pdf (2p), calibration-matrix.xlsx.

Asks: please review and confirm if we should surface this to People Ops (external partner) now or wait until we have pilot pods identified. I want to avoid broad comms until we align on the exception process.

Thanks —
Rachel Kim
Director, Runtime & Serving
Redwood Inference

---

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: rachel.kim@redwood.com
Cc: lauren.bishop@redwood.com, marcus.lin@redwood.com
Date: 2027-05-09 09:05 -07:00
Subject: Re: Proposal: compact pod model + handling performance exceptions

Thanks for the write-up, Rachel — this is thoughtful and feels like the right direction. A couple of quick notes:

1) Pilot: can we nominate 2 pods (one infra-heavy, one product-facing) so we can validate coordination surface reduction?
2) Budget/HC impact: need an ask for recruiting or internal floats for one quarter if we narrow spans; finance will want a short RHS (headcount delta).
3) Calibration window: two weeks seems short for nuanced performance work. Can we structure it as 2 weeks of rapid coaching + optional 30-day follow-up?

I support delaying global comms. Agree we loop People Ops (Maya) but share only the exception process and pilot list for feedback.

-Vivek
VP, Engineering

Good framing — thank you. A few practical asks from partnerships/product side:

- Customer impact: We should flag any customer SLAs/roadmap owners tied to folks in scope; kevin.liu@acme.io is on the vendor pilot and we must protect that relationship. Please add a column in the matrix for "customer criticality."
- Change freeze window: recommend we avoid rewiring reporting during two major launches (June 7–21). Put a constraint in the proposal.
- Comms cadence: a quiet pre-brief to the affected managers, then a one-pager for Exec+CS.

If we keep the 2-week rapid coaching then the 30-day follow-up makes sense. Also +1 to pilot pods.

Lauren
Head of Product Operations

Couple of operational points based on running similar reductions last year:

- Quiet-transition checklist: make it a signed checklist between manager + People Ops so we have auditability. Attach doc template (quiet-transition-checklist.docx).
- Backfill strategy: use internal float bench + 3-month hiring runway; avoid immediate external searches unless role is customer escrow.
- Compensation: any re-banding needs early HR review to avoid comp surprises. We should not change titles as part of the pilot.

I can take ownership of an initial pilot runbook and curate the managers list if you want.

-Marcus
VP, People & Talent (acting)

Thanks for the quick feedback — great points. Next steps I propose: 

1) Marcus to own pilot runbook + managers shortlist (owners: marcus.lin). Target share by 2027-05-14 EOD.
2) Lauren to add customer-criticality column and an execution constraint for June 7–21; update calibration-matrix.xlsx. Target 2027-05-13 noon.
3) Vivek to confirm HC ask template for finance and whether we should reserve 2 internal float hires (target 1 quarter).
4) I'll loop Maya (People Ops partner) to validate the 2-week rapid coaching + 30-day follow-up process and the quiet-transition checklist. Maya — can you review the attached checklist and confirm any minimum legal/notice items we must include for sensitive roles?

Attachments: quiet-transition-checklist.docx, compact-pod-rationale.pdf, calibration-matrix.xlsx

If there's no material legal constraint, we'll kick the pilot (2 pods) the week of 2027-05-24 with a private manager pre-brief. Please reply just with confirmations so I can lock the plan.

Rachel Kim
Director, Runtime & Serving
Redwood Inference
